blinding.reviewed: Eight labelled A/B contact sheets, model reference, and selected original image paths from input-index.json only

criteria: selected accessory presence, placement and quantity
approximate adult model, pose and framing
limitations: One observed output per candidate and case; this does not estimate repeat-run reliability.
Some originals, especially doll, are very small; fine lace and print identity cannot be verified.
Approximate identity and pose assessed visually; no pixel identity claim.
Snake contact sheet shows four selected references; the additional OTHER record in input-index.json was not treated as required.

visible_reasons: A retains the outer jacket's full wrist-length bell sleeves more closely. B shortens them to expose a distinct band of forearm above the hand sleeves.
Both include the navy layered dress, paired bun ornaments and tassels, paired hand sleeves, and buckled chain waist belt.
Both preserve the black jacket's blue-edged collar and embroidered sleeve treatment; A's overall sleeve silhouette is closer to the separate jacket original.
remaining_issues: Both reinterpret the belt's buckles, cords and chains rather than reproduce their exact arrangement.
The hand sleeves overlap the outer jacket, limiting verification of their complete length and lacing.
cases.person_and_hands: Both are plausible adult frontal full-body studio images with the reference boots/background; no obvious gross hand failure at this scale.

visible_reasons: A retains the bonnet's conspicuous pink under-chin ties. B omits them, despite their clear presence in the detailed bonnet original.
Both retain the teal OP's own puffed and flared sleeves, the separate floral wrist cuffs, the bonnet, the bodice heart and the large skirt hearts.
Color, broad lace bands, roses and pink waist bow are close in both; A has the more complete selected accessory construction.
remaining_issues: Both reinterpret the exact skirt heart outlines, lace scallops and lower frill arrangement.
Sleeve and wrist-cuff boundaries blend together somewhat in both.
cases.person_and_hands: Both maintain a plausible adult model and neutral studio framing. Hands remain visible and broadly natural.

visible_reasons: Both include the ivory long-sleeved underblouse, dark cape, witch hat, upper gingham bow and separate waist bow, and the illustrated ivory skirt.
A gives a more curved, decorated cape neckline, while B gives a cleaner open cape silhouette. Neither clearly reproduces the original broad scalloped embroidered cape yoke.
The front/back cape opening and dangling skirt ornaments differ, but the originals do not provide enough frontal construction evidence to rank those differences confidently.
remaining_issues: Both simplify or alter the cape yoke and the exact print and tassel arrangement.
Both make layering readable but do not establish exact construction fidelity.
cases.person_and_hands: Both retain an adult frontal model with visible hands, hat fully in frame, and a consistent studio background.

visible_reasons: B preserves the selected cape as a broad, short, tiered shoulder cape with its large front tie. A turns it into a narrow open shoulder drape and loses most of the characteristic tiered front construction.
B includes a visible neck band with the floral brooch near the collar, more consistent with the dedicated brooch reference.
Both retain the white blouse sleeves, long black gathered skirt and lace veil. B's longer visible veil sides are closer to the long veil original.
remaining_issues: B's cape naturally hides much of the blouse front, so blouse ruffle detail cannot be checked fully.
Exact skirt textile and veil lace motifs remain approximate.
cases.person_and_hands: Both are plausible adult full-body images with natural-looking visible hands and the same broad studio framing.

visible_reasons: B pins the rabbit brooch to the upper side of the chest while keeping the dress's central oval bodice motif visible. A places the rabbit centrally and effectively replaces or covers that native motif.
Both include the lace choker, pink hair bow and matching bonnet, plus the dress's long tiered bell sleeves and horizontal skirt lace bands.
B therefore separates an added selected accessory from the dress's own ornament more successfully.
remaining_issues: The 200px dress reference prevents reliable judgment of fine lace motifs or exact bow quantities.
Both enlarge and reinterpret some pink bow shapes.
cases.person_and_hands: Both keep adult appearance, neutral background and complete head-to-boot framing; hands appear broadly natural.

visible_reasons: Both closely preserve the blue velvet top, keyhole neckline, shoulder ribbons, sheer black hand sleeves, gathered blue skirt and one side floral hair ornament.
B more visibly preserves the flared lace hand-sleeve ends extending over the hands, closer to the original pointed, flaring cuff construction. A's ends are narrower and shorter.
B's front skirt drape is a little broader, closer to the gathered U-shaped blue drape in the skirt original; the difference is modest.
remaining_issues: Both reinterpret bodice buttons, velvet highlights and skirt cords; neither is an exact textile match.
The two outputs are close enough that this is a weak preference and should not alone drive promotion.
cases.person_and_hands: Both maintain adult frontal full-body studio framing. Sleeve lace partly obscures fingers; no obvious extra limb or gross hand failure.

visible_reasons: Both preserve the OP's original black long sleeves, cream collar and floral skirt, and put a cream sleeveless vest and one cameo bow brooch over it.
A retains long cream side ties, which are visible in the detailed vest original. B largely omits their long hanging extent.
Both have broadly similar collar, print and sleeve fidelity; A's extra vest detail provides only a modest advantage.
remaining_issues: Both open and reshape the vest's originally buttoned front.
The vest's long sheer back panel cannot be confirmed from either frontal output; A's long strips do not establish that the complete back layer is present.
The floral print is recognizable in palette and scale but reorganized.
cases.person_and_hands: Both keep plausible adult identity, complete framing and natural visible hands.

visible_reasons: B gives the paired hand sleeves the longer forearm coverage of the original, reaching closer to the elbows. A shortens them and starts them noticeably lower on the forearms.
Both include the paired floral head ornaments and tassels, the white/grey halter bodice, frog closures, front zipper and multiple skirt ruffle tiers.
B retains clearer upper and lower cuff ornament placement, matching the separate long sleeve reference more closely.
remaining_issues: Both reinterpret the cuff's lace motif and small knotted ornaments.
Skirt ruffle shapes and bodice trim are approximate; neither supports an exact detail identity claim.
cases.person_and_hands: Both maintain adult frontal full-body studio framing with unobstructed head ornaments and plausible hands.

strongest_evidence: doll: native bodice motif plus separate brooch
summary.promotion_guidance: Unblind only after freezing this assessment. Compare construction/accessory regressions by case; the aggregate is mixed and does not justify a universal winner from these eight pairs alone.
